parts.article:
The Pyramid of Cestius
 
A 2,000-year-old pyramid in the city of Rome has been restored by archaeologists.
 
(A) Though Rome draws tourists from around the world to its many impressive sites, one notable monument there has never attracted nearly as much interest: the Pyramid of Cestius. But why would there be a pyramid in Italy? After the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 B.C., Egyptian architectural style became the fashion in Rome.
 
(B) Though obelisks and other monuments inspired by Egypt's great pyramids sprang up around the city, only two actual pyramids are known to have been built. The only one left standing, the Pyramid of Cestius, was designed as the burial pyramid for a Roman politician named Caius Cestius, who ordered that the building work be completed within a period of 330 days. Construction took place at some point between 18 B.C. and 12 B.C. Cestius' pyramid had a layer of white Carrara marble on the outside, and was constructed from brick held together by a basic kind of cement on the inside. One of the things that strikes you when you look at the pyramid is how steep it is, so that the shape of Cestius' pyramid is quite unlike that of typical Egyptian ones. This is a difference that could have been the result of inaccurate information sent back to Rome by soldiers who saw the pyramids in person in Egypt. Alternatively, Roman builders could have drawn inspiration from the pyramids in Nubia, a region located in what is today northern Sudan and southern Egypt.
 
(C) At the time of its construction, since there was a strict Roman law prohibiting the placement of tombs within the city itself, the Pyramid of Cestius would have stood in the countryside. Rome grew enormously during the next two centuries, and, by the 3rd century A.D., the pyramid would have been surrounded by buildings. We also know that in the 3rd century A.D., the Pyramid of Cestius was hidden behind a high wall on the orders of Emperor Aurelian; this probably helped it survive throughout the centuries to come, even as other ancient monuments disappeared. By the Middle Ages, the pyramid was covered in vegetation and thick dirt, and popular myth had developed that it might be a tomb for one of the twin brothers Romulus and Remus, who were regarded as the men who had established the city of Rome. Cestius' actual tomb within the pyramid and the inscription identifying the pyramid as his weren't rediscovered until the 1660s, when the pyramid underwent restoration. During excavations, when trees and plants were cleared away, two marble bases were found in front of the pyramid, as well as fragments of bronze statues that had once stood on them, on either side of the pyramid. The people employed to excavate the pyramid did not find the urn that would have contained Cestius' remains, but they did come across a tunnel. It was quite possible, therefore, that robbers had at some earlier time removed the contents of the tomb. But while some of the features of Cestius' tomb no longer exist, at least the pyramid itself has survived.
 
(D) Today, the foundations of Cestius' pyramid rest below street level near an intersection with heavy traffic, so that passing tourists and residents could easily fail to notice its full height of 119 feet. Across the intersection is the Piramide station, located on Line B of the Rome Metro. In 2011, the Japanese clothing-company entrepreneur Yuzo Yagi, president of Yagi Tsusho Ltd, announced his intention to help the Italian government pay for an ambitious renovation of the Pyramid of Cestius. 'It's an act of gratitude,' he later told journalists. 'Our company has grown thanks to Italy.' Work began at the site shortly after Yagi signed an official agreement with the Special Superintendency for the Archaeological Heritage of Rome, and was completed ahead of schedule thanks to his 2-million-euro contribution.
 
(E) As archaeologist Leonardo Guarnieri explained to journalists, officials are now conducting tours of the newly renovated pyramid twice a month by reservation. Visitors who take advantage of the tour can make their way through a narrow corridor in order to enter the burial chamber itself. It is within these walls that they can admire the frescoes: watercolour paintings typical of the time. In the chamber, it is possible to make out four frescoes of the winged Roman goddess of war, Victoria, a figure from Roman legend, as well as a series of vases, the type that would have been used for special rituals and purification purposes. We know from the writings of earlier visitors that there used to be more here, but the majority have disappeared over time. Only one problem remains now that the restoration is complete. The white exterior of the Pyramid of Cestius will have to be cleaned every few months to remove the layer of urban pollution. A team of free-climbers will be employed to do the job, in order to avoid placing builders' scaffolding around the newly welcoming monument.

Questions 1–7
Do the following statements agree with the information in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–7 on your answer sheet, write:

Q1 The Pyramid of Cestius has always been one of Rome's most popular tourist attractions.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 The construction of the Pyramid was completed before Cestius' death.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 In the Middle Ages, people thought an original founder of Rome was buried in the Pyramid of Cestius.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 Today, the height of the Pyramid is something that tourists and residents immediately notice.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 Japanese businessman Yuzo Yagi was an admirer of both Italian and Egyptian architecture.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 The restoration of the Pyramid of Cestius, which was funded by Yuzo Yagi, finished earlier than expected.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 Most of the original frescoes inside Cestius' tomb have survived to this day.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

干扰 千万别只看到“Rome draws tourists（罗马吸引游客）”就选True，要看后半句对这个特定景点的否定描述。

句子 (A) Though Rome draws tourists from around the world to its many impressive sites, one notable monument there has never attracted nearly as much interest: the Pyramid of Cestius.

解析 文章第一段明确说，尽管罗马吸引了全世界的游客，但这座金字塔“never attracted nearly as much interest（从未吸引过哪怕接近那么多的兴趣）”，也就是说它并不怎么受关注。

Q2

解析 文中只提到Cestius“ordered（下令）”金字塔在330天内完工，但并没有说他在完工时是活着还是已经去世了。

干扰 你可能觉得既然是陵墓（burial pyramid）肯定死后才用，或者既然是他下令的肯定生前就在建，但文中没有明确的时间对比，不要脑补。

句子 (B) The only one left standing, the Pyramid of Cestius, was designed as the burial pyramid for a Roman politician named Caius Cestius, who ordered that the building work be completed within a period of 330 days.

Q3

解析 文中提到中世纪时有一个流行的传言（popular myth），认为这是Romulus或Remus的墓，而这两人被视为“established the city of Rome（建立了罗马城的人）”，即创始人。

干扰 题目把具体的人名（Romulus and Remus）替换成了他们的身份（founder of Rome），只要能对应上就是对的。

句子 （C段）： By the Middle Ages, ...popular myth had developed that it might be a tomb for one of the twin brothers Romulus and Remus, who were regarded as the men who had established the city of Rome.

Q4

干扰 一定要看到“fail to”这个否定词组，不要看到“notice”就觉得意思一致。

解析 文中说由于地基低于街道水平且交通繁忙，路人很容易“fail to notice（没注意到）”它的全高，这与题目中的“immediately notice（立即注意到）”意思相反。

句子 (D) Today, the foundations of Cestius' pyramid rest below street level near an intersection with heavy traffic, so that passing tourists and residents could easily fail to notice its full height of 119 feet.

Q5

解析 文中只提到Yuzo Yagi出于“gratitude（感激）”资助修复，因为他的公司得益于意大利的发展，完全没提他是否欣赏埃及建筑。

干扰 不要因为文章主题是金字塔（埃及风格）就觉得赞助人一定喜欢埃及建筑，文中没说就是没说。

句子 （D段）： 'It's an act of gratitude,' he later told journalists. 'Our company has grown thanks to Italy.'

Q6

解析 文中说修复工作“completed ahead of schedule（在计划时间之前完成）”，这与题目中的“finished earlier than expected”是完美的同义替换。

干扰 这题非常直接，只要认识“ahead of schedule”就不会错。

句子 （D段）： Work began at the site shortly after Yagi signed an official agreement... and was completed ahead of schedule thanks to his 2-million-euro contribution.

Q7

句子 （E段）： We know from the writings of earlier visitors that there used to be more here, but the majority have disappeared over time.

干扰 注意数量词的对比，“majority”对应“most”，但动作是相反的（disappeared vs survived）。

解析 文中明确指出虽然还有一些壁画，但“the majority have disappeared（绝大多数已经消失了）”，这与题目的“Most... survived（大部分存活）”直接矛盾。

Q8

解析 定位到B段关于材料的描述，文中提到外面是marble，里面是“constructed from brick（由砖块建造）”并用水泥粘合。

干扰 题目中有“cement and marble”作为定位词，剩下的那个材料就是brick。注意只能填一个词，不要加s（原文是单数概念brick）。

句子 （B段）： Cestius' pyramid had a layer of white Carrara marble on the outside, and was constructed from brick held together by a basic kind of cement on the inside.

Q9

解析 文中提到金字塔非常陡峭，所以它的“shape（形状）”和典型的埃及金字塔很不通过。

干扰 题目中的“different”对应文中的“quite unlike”。

句子 （B段）： One of the things that strikes you when you look at the pyramid is how steep it is, so that the shape of Cestius' pyramid is quite unlike that of typical Egyptian ones.

Q10

句子 （C段）： At the time of its construction, since there was a strict Roman law prohibiting the placement of tombs within the city itself, the Pyramid of Cestius would have stood in the countryside.

解析 文中解释说因为法律禁止在城内建墓，所以当时它建在“countryside（乡下/郊外）”。

干扰 定位词是“forbidden（禁止）”，对应文中的“prohibiting”。

Q11

解析 定位到C段的1660s修复部分，文中说发现了底座以及“fragments of bronze statues（青铜雕像的碎片）”。

干扰 题目中的“broken”对应文中的“fragments of”（碎片/残片）。

句子 （C段）： During excavations... two marble bases were found in front of the pyramid, as well as fragments of bronze statues that had once stood on them...

Q12

解析 文中说挖掘者没有找到骨灰瓮，但他们发现了“tunnel（隧道/地道）”，因此推测是盗墓贼干的。

干扰 这道题逻辑是：发现了什么 -> 推导出有盗贼。文中的逻辑链正是：come across a tunnel -> possible that robbers...

句子 （C段）： The people employed to excavate the pyramid did not find the urn... but they did come across a tunnel. It was quite possible, therefore, that robbers had at some earlier time removed the contents of the tomb.

Q13

解析 文章最后一段提到，需要攀爬者（free-climbers）来清除“layer of urban pollution（城市污染层）”。

干扰 题目中的“get rid of”对应文中的“remove”。

句子 （E段）： The white exterior of the Pyramid of Cestius will have to be cleaned every few months to remove the layer of urban pollution.
